title: Reliability patterns: circuit breakers, graceful degradation, health checks

claims.text: Basiri and colleagues set out the discipline in IEEE Software in 2016, volume 33, pages 35 to 41, arguing that modern software-based services are distributed systems with complex behaviour and failure modes, and that verifying reliability requires experimentation rather than reasoning alone.

source.title: Ali Basiri, Niosha Behnam, Ruud de Rooij, Lorin Hochstein, Luke Kosewski, Justin Reynolds and Casey Rosenthal, Chaos Engineering, IEEE Software 33(3):35-41, May 2016, doi 10.1109/MS.2016.60 (preprint arXiv:1702.05843)

claims.text: Their experimental method has four steps: define the steady state of the system to set a baseline for normal behaviour; hypothesise that this steady state will continue in both the control and the experimental groups; introduce variables reflecting real-world events such as server crashes, disk malfunctions or severed network connections; then try to disprove the hypothesis by looking for a difference between the groups. If the steady state is hard to disrupt the system is robust, and if there is a weakness you have something to fix.

source.title: Ali Basiri, Niosha Behnam, Ruud de Rooij, Lorin Hochstein, Luke Kosewski, Justin Reynolds and Casey Rosenthal, Chaos Engineering, IEEE Software 33(3):35-41, May 2016, doi 10.1109/MS.2016.60 (preprint arXiv:1702.05843)

claims.text: Their canonical steady-state measure is a business metric rather than a technical one: the rate at which customers press play on a streaming device, called streams per second. The paper notes that business metrics are often better suited to measuring customer experience than technical ones are.

source.title: Ali Basiri, Niosha Behnam, Ruud de Rooij, Lorin Hochstein, Luke Kosewski, Justin Reynolds and Casey Rosenthal, Chaos Engineering, IEEE Software 33(3):35-41, May 2016, doi 10.1109/MS.2016.60 (preprint arXiv:1702.05843)

beats.broke: a system made of many parts has failure modes nobody enumerated, and the ones that matter are discovered during incidents rather than during design
beats.fix: stop reasoning about failure and start inducing it — define what normal looks like as a measurable quantity, hypothesise it survives a specific injected fault, and look for a difference
beats.cost: the experiment has to run where the behaviour is real, so the practice is only as safe as the blast radius you can bound, and defining normal as a number is harder than it sounds
beats.interview: what you would measure to know whether a reliability mechanism actually works
